summary: A reporter recounts living through a major power outage in a city on September 15th, 2023, and investigates its causes and prevention. Electrical engineer Dr. Sandra Keaton describes aging infrastructure, severe weather, solar storms, human error and cyber attacks as key risks. City Energy Commissioner Alex Torres outlines upgrades, vegetation management, grid modernization, cybersecurity and community preparedness as responses.
one_line: A reporter's account of the September 15th, 2023 city blackout, with expert views on outage causes and the city's prevention measures.
key_facts: A major power outage struck the city in the early hours of September 15th, 2023, affecting several neighborhoods and halting daily activities.
Dr. Sandra Keaton, an electrical engineer, was interviewed on September 20th about why outages still happen.

Dr. Keaton said aging infrastructure is among the top causes of outages: "much of our grid was designed and built decades ago and isn't equipped to handle the increased load from today's hyper-connected society."
A thunderstorm preceded the city's blackout; downed trees, flooding and lightning strikes routinely overwhelm power lines, transformers and substations.
On October 3rd, 2023, a solar storm triggered geomagnetic interruptions, matching National Space and Atmospheric Administration reports on solar activity's potential impact on power systems.
On November 8th, maintenance at a local substation went awry due to miscommunication, causing an outage across three neighborhoods.
Dr. Keaton warned of cyber threats, saying "Our grid is smarter, yes, but that also makes it a target for digital threats."
On December 12th of the previous year, hackers infiltrated a utility network and caused outages.
City Energy Commissioner Alex Torres was interviewed on December 18th, 2023 about preventive steps.
Torres highlighted the transition from traditional to smart grids with real-time monitoring and self-healing capabilities, plus more weather-resistant materials.
The city started a rigorous vegetation management program, trimming trees near power lines to prevent outages from falling branches.
Torres said integrating renewable sources like solar and wind diversifies electricity supply and reduces the risk of widespread outages.
Cybersecurity measures mentioned by Torres include regular audits, staff training and rapid response teams.
Torres urged individuals to have emergency kits and plans, saying "A well-informed and prepared public is a resilient one."
